I found no dated AI predictions by Satya Nadella from 2016 that I can quote. Treat that as "not verified," not as "nothing exists." The likely 2016 sources came up in search, but my own coding mistake meant I never read their text.

**What went wrong:** I used all six page openings on Microsoft's official transcripts for Build 2016 (30 March), Envision 2016, Worldwide Partner Conference 2016 and Ignite 2016 (26 September). I also used them on Nadella's Slate essay of 28 June and Fast Company's 27 September interview. My script misread whatever came back, recorded each page as an error with no error code, and threw the text away. When I tried again I was told I had no page openings left. So I don't know whether the pages actually opened, and I have read none of them. Every quote I could give would come from a search snippet, so I give none.

**What the snippets suggest (checker leads, not findings):**
* 2016 was about "Conversation as a Platform" (bots and Cortana) and "democratizing AI." The snippets I saw were framed as visions and had no dates.
* Fortune's paraphrase says Nadella hopes to have the National Football League (NFL) fantasy football chat app ready "by the next football season." That is a product launch date, reported only by Fortune and only seen in a snippet, so I left it out.
* Bloomberg's 2016 Nadella interview and two YouTube videos labelled Davos/World Economic Forum turned up but were not opened. The YouTube videos carry no 2016 date. On the Bloomberg page, only the address shows 2016.

I used 9 of 12 searches and stopped, since I had no way left to read any page.
